cleanIntro: Knight's own instruction is to clean and lubricate after every day's shooting. Black powder and its approved substitutes are corrosive and deposit residue in the bore, breech plug, hammer, receiver and trigger — stainless included, which is more corrosion resistant than blued steel but is not corrosion proof.

steps.title: Prove the bore is empty
steps.action: Run the maker's three checks before touching anything else on the TK2000. Safeties to safe and working, no primer in the receiver live or spent, then stand it on its butt and drop the ramrod down the bore. A ramrod tip near flush with the muzzle is your only proof there is no charge; a tip standing proud means it is still loaded.
steps.quote: 1.) Confirm that all safeties are functioning properly and are in the safe position. 2.) Check that there is no primer, either live or spent, installed. 3.) Place the rifle butt on the ground, remove the ramrod, and place it in the bore. If the ramrod tip is near flush with the muzzle, the rifle is unloaded and the bore free from obstruction. Remove the ramrod from the barrel.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Loading and Firing, Preparing to Load — p.11
steps.warn: There is no extractor and no ejection port. The ramrod depth check is the unloaded check.

steps.title: Confirm again before any solvent
steps.action: Knight repeats this at the head of the cleaning section, and on a shotgun that has been carried loaded it is the check that matters. Hot water, solvent and a bore brush all put force down a barrel that may still hold a charge.
steps.quote: WARNING! Before cleaning, be certain that the rifle is unloaded and that no primer is in the receiver. Cleaning a loaded or primed rifle may result in accidental discharge.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning — p.9
steps.warn: Cleaning a loaded or primed firearm may result in accidental discharge.

steps.title: Know which action you are working on
steps.action: The TK2000 is a straight-pull, not a bolt gun. Its hammer assembly comes out of the back of the receiver as a unit once the end cap is off — there is no bolt and no bolt-release detent. If you are reading a Knight procedure that talks about lifting a bolt handle, you are in the wrong section of the book.
steps.caution: Do not use the bolt-action strip from the other half of this manual. It is a different mechanism.
steps.quote: Action: Patented Double Safety System, one-piece removable Extreme 209 hammer assembly. Removable stainless steel breech plug (see page 22 for breech plug identification).
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — TK2000 Shotgun — p.40

steps.title: How the straight pull works
steps.action: Pull the hammer assembly rearward out of the receiver until it cocks. With both safeties off, the trigger releases the hammer, which runs forward through the receiver and strikes the primer in line with the bore. Understanding that the hammer travels inside the receiver is what makes the end-cap step make sense.
steps.quote: The pull type system functions by pulling the hammer assembly back from the receiver until it cocks.With both safeties off, the hammer under the spring tension is released with a pull of the trigger.The hammer slides through the receiver and strikes the primer.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Action and Safety Systems, Straight Pull Action — p.44

steps.title: Set up before you break anything down
steps.action: Padded vise and a parts tray first. The breech plug can need real force to start and the barrel needs supporting while you apply it. The letters in the steps below — (O), (S9), (W), (D), (I) — are the manual's schematic labels, so keep the schematic to hand.
steps.quote: It is advisable to use a padded vise to remove and reinstall the breech plug. Place small parts in a pan to avoid losing them.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly — p.45

steps.title: Ramrod out
steps.action: Draw the ramrod (O) from under the forend and set it aside before you go near the stock screw. It must be out before the barrelled action will lift clear.
steps.quote: 1.) Remove the ramrod (O) from the stock and set aside.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.45

steps.title: Barrelled action out of the stock
steps.action: A single stock screw (S9) just forward of the trigger guard (W) holds everything together. Back it right out, then lift the barrel and receiver away from the stock (R) rather than levering — the inletting chips easily.
steps.quote: 2.) Remove the barreled action from the stock.The barreled action is held in the stock by a single stock screw (S9) located just forward of the trigger guard (W). Remove this screw and carefully separate the barrel assembly from the stock (R). Set the stock aside.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.45

steps.title: Trigger assembly off
steps.action: One mounting screw releases the trigger assembly as a unit; lift it straight off the receiver. Do not take the assembly itself apart — it is cleaned as a unit, and with solvent only.
steps.quote: 3.) Remove the trigger assembly. Remove the trigger mounting screw (7), and lift the trigger assembly from the receiver.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.45

steps.title: End cap off, hammer assembly out backwards
steps.action: This is the step that separates this action from every bolt-action Knight. Unscrew the end cap (D) anticlockwise off the rear of the receiver, then draw the hammer assembly straight back and out. The hammer spring is captive in the assembly, but keep a hand on it as the cap comes free rather than letting it spring loose.
steps.caution: The hammer assembly is under spring tension. Control the end cap as it releases.
steps.quote: 4.) Remove the hammer assembly. Unscrew the end cap (D) in a counter-clockwise direction. Pull the hammer assembly backward removing the hammer from the receiver.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.45

steps.title: Soap and water, but read the label
steps.action: Black powder and its substitutes are corrosive and must come off the same day. Hot soapy water or an approved solvent — but no chlorides, no lye, no bleach, all of which strip bluing. Stainless is more corrosion resistant than blued steel and still is not corrosion proof.
steps.quote: 2.) Clean rifle with soap and water or an approved solvent. Do not use soaps with chlorides, lye, or bleach in them; the chemicals may remove blueing on your barrel.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: TK2000 trigger: solvent only, never water
steps.action: Knight names the TK2000 explicitly in this instruction, so there is no ambiguity about whether it applies. The breech plug and the hammer go into hot soapy water; the trigger assembly never does. Clean it with solvent, wipe it, oil the sear. And do not leave any part soaking while you do something else.
steps.quote: 3.) Clean your rifle from the breech end. Place your breech plug and hammer in hot soapy water or Knight® Solvent™. Do not use water to clean triggers for DISC Extreme™, Long Range Hunter™, Peregrine™, Mountaineer™, Bighorn™, Littlehorn™, and TK2000™. Only a solvent should be used to clean these Knight Rifles. Clean with appropriate material and lubricate sear. Don’t allow barreled action and other rifle parts to soak in soapy water or solvents for extended periods.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10
steps.warn: Never put the trigger assembly in water. Solvent only.

steps.title: Scrub the bore from the breech end
steps.action: With the plug out, clean the shotgun the way it was designed to be cleaned — breech to muzzle, so fouling leaves the bore instead of being pushed back into the breech. Muzzle in the hot water, patch on the jag at the rear of the receiver, push through, and repeat until a patch comes out clean.
steps.quote: 4.) Use a Knight® Ultimate Range Rod™ or a ramrod with a Knight® Bullet Starter™ handle and an attached cleaning jag.With the muzzle still in the hot soapy water, place a patch over the rear of the receiver and push into the barrel. Scrub the bore vigorously to completely remove all foreign matter, powder residue, and fouling. Repeat this as many times as necessary to get a clean bore.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: Detail the receiver and hammer
steps.action: A toothbrush and pipe cleaners reach what a patch cannot: inside the receiver where the hammer runs, the hammer body itself, the plug, and around the trigger. The hammer runs the full length of the receiver on this action, so the receiver bore collects fouling along its whole length rather than just at the breech.
steps.quote: 6.) Using a toothbrush or pipe cleaner, thoroughly clean the receiver, hammer, breech plug, trigger and other components of all residues, fouling, etc.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: Dry completely, then oil generously
steps.action: Water cleaning only works if the drying is total, inside and out. Bore, receiver interior, plug threads, the underside of the barrel where it sat in the stock — dry them all, then oil with a water-displacing rust inhibitor.
steps.quote: 7.) Thoroughly dry all metal surfaces and generously lubricate your rifle inside and out using Knight® Oil™ with rust inhibitor.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

steps.title: 12 gauge bore, and what must never go down it
steps.action: The TK2000 is a 26 inch 12 gauge barrel with internal jug choking — the constriction is machined into the bore rather than screwed in, so there is no choke tube to remove and no tube threads to clean. Brush the jug section as part of the bore and check it is dry; a bore that steps in and out like this traps water at the step.
steps.quote: Barrel: 26” 12 gauge with internal jug choking.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — TK2000 Shotgun — p.40

steps.title: Never load this barrel with pellets
steps.action: Worth knowing at cleaning time because it explains what you will and will not find in the bore. Pelletised powder does not fit a 12 gauge bore properly and Knight forbids it outright — if you find pellet residue or an unburnt pellet while cleaning, something has been loaded that should not have been.
steps.quote: Do not use pelletized powder, it does not fit the 12 gauge bore properly and can cause an explosion, delayed ignition, or no ignition.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Loading Instructions for the TK2000™ Muzzleloading Shotgun — p.15
steps.warn: Never load pelletized powder in the TK2000. It can cause an explosion, delayed ignition, or no ignition.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The TK2000 is now down to its owner-level groups: stock, barrelled action, trigger assembly and hammer assembly, with the bore and receiver cleaned and oiled. From here you either reassemble in the manual's order, or go on to Deep Clean for the breech plug.
steps.quote: 8.) Reassemble your muzzleloader according to the instructions in your model’s section of this manual.
steps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

deepSteps.title: Breech plug out
deepSteps.action: Barrel in the padded vise. Engage the plug (I) with the breech plug wrench end of the combo tool through the rear of the receiver and turn anticlockwise. A plug that has been fired and not greased can take serious force — the combo tool is drilled so a rod can be passed through for leverage.
deepSteps.caution: Use a padded vise. Levering on an unsupported barrel marks it.
deepSteps.quote: 5.) Remove the breech plug. Insert the combo tool (breech plug wrench side) into the receiver, engage the breech plug (I) and turn it counter-clockwise.This may require a considerable amount of force. (Holes in the combo tool allow a rod to be used for added leverage).
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Disassembly — p.45

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug threads in the receiver
deepSteps.action: The female threads in the receiver hold the worst of the baked-on fouling, and a plug torqued onto that fouling is what seizes. Toothbrush for the outer threads, a bullet starter with adapter and a 20 gauge shotgun brush for full depth.
deepSteps.quote: 5.) Thoroughly scrub and clean the breech plug threads in the receiver. A toothbrush, bottle brush, or bullet starter with adapter and 20 gauge shotgun brush work well for this task.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Care and Cleaning, Instructions for Cleaning — p.10

deepSteps.title: Breech plug back in, greased
deepSteps.action: Grease the plug threads before it goes near the receiver — that is what stops it seizing next time. Run it in with the combo tool, hand tighten until firm against the back of the barrel and fully home. Hand tight is the specification; over-tightening is explicitly what makes it hard to remove.
deepSteps.caution: Hand tight only. Do not overtighten the plug.
deepSteps.quote: 1.) Install the breech plug. Fill the threads of the plug with Knight® Breech Plug Grease™ to help prevent the breech plug from sticking in the receiver. Using the breech plug end of the combo tool, insert the breech plug (I) into the rear of the receiver and hand tighten the plug into the receiver until it is firmly against the back of the barrel. Be sure the breech plug is screwed all the way into the receiver. Do not overtighten the plug or it will become difficult to remove.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Assembly — p.45

deepSteps.title: Trigger back on
deepSteps.action: Mount the trigger assembly (Q) with its screw (S7) and tighten until it sits firm and square against the receiver. It has to be aligned before the hammer goes back in, or the sear will not pick the hammer up.
deepSteps.quote: 2.) Install the trigger. Using the trigger mounting screw (S7), mount the trigger assembly (Q) to the receiver.Tighten until the trigger assembly is firm against the receiver. Make sure it is aligned with the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Assembly — p.45

deepSteps.title: Hammer assembly in, trigger held back
deepSteps.action: This is the one piece of sequence that is easy to get wrong. Put the trigger safety forward to fire, hold the trigger back so the sear drops out of the way, and slide the hammer assembly (A) in past it. Then screw the end cap (D) home finger tight. If the hammer will not pass, the sear is still up — you have not held the trigger back.
deepSteps.caution: The end cap is finger tight, not wrenched.
deepSteps.quote: 3.) Install the hammer. Place the trigger safety in the forward fire position.While pulling the trigger back, slide the hammer assembly (A) into the receiver and past the trigger sear. Screw the end cap (D) clockwise into place, finger tight.
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Assembly — p.45

deepSteps.title: Barrel back in the stock, ramrod home
deepSteps.action: Drop the barrelled action back into the stock and tighten the stock screw (S9), then return the ramrod (O) to its thimbles. Check the safeties work in both positions before the gun goes away.
deepSteps.quote: 4.) Install the barrel and stock. Place the barreled action into the stock and tighten the stock screw (S9). Install the ramrod (O).
deepSteps.cite: Knight Rifles Owner's Manual — 2024 edition; no edition code, revision or copyright line printed anywhere (identified by sha256) — Disassembly and Assembly, Assembly — p.45

cleaning.name: Barrel and breech
tasks: Scrub the bore breech-to-muzzle with a wet patch until patches come out clean
Scrub the breech plug threads in the receiver with a brush that reaches full depth
Clean the breech plug body and its flash channel
Dry the bore completely, then run an oiled patch through

cleaning.name: Hammer assembly and receiver
tasks: Wash the breech plug and hammer in hot soapy water or Knight solvent
Brush the full length of the receiver bore the hammer travels down
Clean and dry the end cap threads and its O-ring seat
Dry every wetted surface, then oil with a water-displacing rust inhibitor

cleaning.name: Trigger group — solvent only
tasks: Clean the trigger assembly with solvent, never water
Do not leave the assembly soaking in solvent

cleaning.name: Stock and exterior
tasks: Wipe solvent and water off the stock before it soaks in
Check the stock screw hole and recoil area are dry
Wipe all exterior metal with an oiled cloth

reassembly: Grease the breech plug threads and hand tighten the plug fully home — hand tight only.
Mount the trigger assembly with its screw and check it is aligned with the receiver.
Trigger safety forward to fire, hold the trigger back, and slide the hammer assembly in past the sear.
Screw the end cap on finger tight.
Set the barrelled action into the stock and tighten the stock screw.
Return the ramrod to the stock.
fncheck: Before loading, clear the breech plug flash channel of cleaning oil: fit a primer, point the muzzle at the ground four to six inches from dirt or grass, and fire the primer. The dirt should visibly move — that is the channel proving clear. Repeat once, remove the spent primer, and return both safeties to safe. Then swab the bore with a wet patch and a dry patch, each contacting the breech plug, before the first charge.
